_README: Copy to ~/.claude-bridge/accounts.json (or point CLAUDE_BRIDGE_ACCOUNTS at it).
Each account is a Claude Code CONFIG DIRECTORY that is already logged in.
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is the only working credential override, so an account IS
a config dir. Create one and log into it interactively, once:
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-acct1 claude auth login
Nothing is copied between machines. Each machine logs itself in, so a
credential never travels and a machine can only ever hold its own.
mode:
work  — only accounts with scope "local": this machine's own. Byte-for-
byte today's behaviour when exactly one is listed.
pool  — local accounts FIRST, then shared ones. The local account has one
consumer, so draining it first minimises contention with any other
machine by construction: a shared account is reached only when
this machine has nothing of its own left.
scope:
local  — this machine owns it. No other machine spends its budget.
shared — the same Anthropic account is also used elsewhere (e.g. the PVE
pool). Routing state is PER MACHINE, so a cap another machine hit
is discovered here by one failed turn, not in advance. That one
wasted turn is the entire price of not running a distributed
lease, which would add a stuck-lease failure mode that does not
exist today.
(absent) — treated as local. A config written before modes existed
describes one machine's own account; reading it as shared would
silently enrol it in a pool it was never meant to join.
Delete the _README key or leave it — unknown keys are ignored.
